palette: ONE PULSE, ONE PHRASE, ONE DRONE. A small, close, modern chamber score: felt-muted upright piano, low strings (cellos, violas; a few violins high and soft), cello pizzicato, a dark airy synth pad, and a slow low brass swell used once (the title). Three ideas carry the whole film. THE PULSE (M1): a low muted heartbeat on D at 76 bpm (felt piano low note doubled by cello pizzicato), the sound of the trap closing; it builds the cold open, stops dead on YES, returns at the baggage belt and stops at the discovery; in the wait it comes back at half speed, distant. THE PRIZE (M2): four felt-piano notes, A C F E, warm in F major in Chicago; the same four notes over D minor in chapter 3, when the gift turns cold, as YES means two things; fragments in the last chapters; and its first note alone at the very end. THE DRONE (M4): low D and A, the Void Stage, made locally as sound design so the exact same sound can return at the end. The travel tick (M3) is the pulse in disguise: a high, light 84 bpm tick in Hong Kong that moves lower and darker until it is the pulse at the belt ("a tick that becomes the gate"). RULES: no drums, no kit, no vocals, no choir, no risers, braams or hits in the score (the two low impacts are effects); entries come in from nothing under the end of the shot before and rise; exits are designed (the script's hard stops, or natural decay), never a fade under a line that matters; never cut to the beat; everything in tune at A = 440, measured and retuned within 5 cents; prompts name no sound effects, no drugs, no violence, no existing works.

key_map: Home key D minor (A = 440). Cold open: D minor, the pulse on D. Ch 01-02: F major, the relative major (warmth), with a Lydian lift in Hong Kong. Ch 03: F major turning to D minor under the same four notes. Ch 04: D minor, the pulse; after the discovery a low D with E-flat above. Ch 05: unscored (the clock is the score). Ch 06: D minor thinning to a held A. Ch 07: D minor, spare. Ch 08: B-flat major moving to D minor. Ch 09: D minor; the last note is A over the D drone: an open fifth with no third, neither major nor minor, unresolved. The drone (D2 73.42 Hz, A2 110 Hz) and the impacts (pitched to D1) sit in the same key.
arc: Cold open: from no music, a low D rises, the pulse builds, stops dead on YES; silence; it rebuilds to "were not" and is cut dead; impact, rain, near silence; the title builds from nothing to the film's first peak and decays to silence. Ch 01-02: warmth (piano, the prize), then light motion (the tick). Ch 03: the warmth turns; the pulse returns at the belt. Ch 04: the pulse to the discovery, hard stop, then a cold held note. Ch 05: no score, a clock. Ch 06: one low impact, grave strings thinning to one note, silence. Ch 07-09: spare piano, long holds, silence at the strongest lines; total silence for the empty chair; the drone returns and one warm note ends it.
intensity_targets: Loudest score: the title peak (about the voice's level, 0 dB re voice, in a stretch with no voice). Under the voice: -14 (the pulse in the cold open) to -24 dB re voice (the last chapters). The mix masters to -14 LUFS with an LRA of 7 LU or more: the quiet last four minutes are what make the range.
